arxiv-2205-14821.title: LAMOST MRS-N Observations of the W80 Region
arxiv-2205-14821.creator: Yao Li, Chao-Jian Wu, Yong-Qiang Yao, Wei Zhang, Jia Yin, Juan-Juan Ren, Chih-Hao Hsia, Rui Zhuang, Jian-Jun Chen, Yu-Zhong Wu, Hui Zhu, Bin Li, Yong-Hui Hou, Meng-Yuan Yao, Hong Wu
arxiv-2205-14821.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Yao Li, Chao-Jian Wu, Yong-Qiang Yao, Wei Zhang, Jia Yin, Juan-Juan Ren, Chih-Hao Hsia, Rui Zhuang, Jian-Jun Chen, Yu-Zhong Wu, Hui Zhu, Bin Li, Yong-Hui Hou, Meng-Yuan Yao, Hong Wu. The spectral observations and analysis for the W80 Region are presented by using the data of Medium-Resolution Spectroscopic Survey of Nebulae (MRS-N) with the Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopy Telescope (LAMOST).

arxiv-2305-12480.title: Is Translation Helpful? An Empirical Analysis of Cross-Lingual Transfer in Low-Resource Dialog Generation
arxiv-2305-12480.creator: Lei Shen, Shuai Yu, Xiaoyu Shen
arxiv-2305-12480.description: Abstract Cross-lingual transfer is important for developing high-quality chatbots in multiple languages due to the strongly imbalanced distribution of language resources. A typical approach is to leverage off-the-shelf machine translation (MT) systems to utilize either the training corpus or developed models from high-resource languages.

arxiv-2407-17622.title: Towards Neural Network based Cognitive Models of Dynamic Decision-Making by Humans
arxiv-2407-17622.creator: Changyu Chen, Shashank Reddy Chirra, Maria José Ferreira, Cleotilde Gonzalez, Arunesh Sinha, Pradeep Varakantham
arxiv-2407-17622.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Changyu Chen, Shashank Reddy Chirra, Maria José Ferreira, Cleotilde Gonzalez, Arunesh Sinha, Pradeep Varakantham. Modeling human cognitive processes in dynamic decision-making tasks has been an endeavor in AI for a long time because such models can help make AI systems more intuitive, personalized, mitigate any human biases, and enhance training in simulation. Some initial work has attempted to utilize neural networks (and large language models) but often assumes one common model for all humans and aims to emulate human behavior in aggregate.

arxiv-2408-08948.title: Accidental Suppression of Wilson Coefficients in Higgs Coupling
arxiv-2408-08948.creator: Yunjia Bao, Jiayin Gu, Zhen Liu, Chi Shu, Lian-Tao Wang
arxiv-2408-08948.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yunjia Bao, Jiayin Gu, Zhen Liu, Chi Shu, Lian-Tao Wang. Higgs couplings are essential probes for physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM) since they can be modified by new physics, such as through the Higgs portal interaction | H | 2 ​ 𝒪 |H|^{2}\mathcal{O} . These modifications influence Higgs interactions via dimension-6 operators of the form ( ∂ | H | 2 ) 2 \left(\partial|H|^{2}\right)^{2} and | H | 6 |H|^{6} , which are generally expected to be of comparable size.

arxiv-2412-04404.title: Federated Automated Feature Engineering
arxiv-2412-04404.creator: Tom Overman 1 , Diego Klabjan 2
arxiv-2412-04404.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tom Overman 1 , Diego Klabjan 2. 1 Abstract Automated feature engineering (AutoFE) is used to automatically create new features from original features to improve predictive performance without needing significant human intervention and domain expertise. Many algorithms exist for AutoFE, but very few approaches exist for the federated learning (FL) setting where data is gathered across many clients and is not shared between clients or a central server.

arxiv-2501-06326.title: On Creating A Brain-To-Text Decoder
arxiv-2501-06326.creator: Zenon Lamprou, Yashar Moshfeghi
arxiv-2501-06326.description: Abstract Brain decoding has emerged as a rapidly advancing and extensively utilized technique within neuroscience. This paper centers on the application of raw electroencephalogram (EEG) signals for decoding human brain activity, offering a more expedited and efficient methodology for enhancing our understanding of the human brain.

arxiv-2507-03741.title: Evaluating an Embryo Origin for Detached TNOs within Full Kuiper Belt Formation Models
arxiv-2507-03741.creator: Nathan A. Kaib, Chadwick A. Trujillo, Scott S. Sheppard
arxiv-2507-03741.description: Abstract With perihelia well beyond Neptune, but semimajor axes and eccentricities indicative of substantial perturbation, the origins of detached trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs) remain a dynamical puzzle. In particular, detached TNOs with orbital inclinations below ∼ \sim 25 ∘ are not easily generated from any known mechanism currently in the modern solar system.

arxiv-2511-00378.title: Modeling Uncertainty in Integrated Assessment Models
arxiv-2511-00378.creator: Yongyang Cai
arxiv-2511-00378.description: Abstract Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs) are pivotal tools that synthesize knowledge from climate science, economics, and policy to evaluate the interactions between human activities and the climate system. They serve as essential instruments for policymakers, providing insights into the potential outcomes of various climate policies and strategies.

europmc-pmc3932552.title: The default mode network and social understanding of others: what do brain connectivity studies tell us.
europmc-pmc3932552.creator: Li W, Mai X, Liu C.
europmc-pmc3932552.description: The Default Mode Network (DMN) has been found to be involved in various domains of cognitive and social processing. The present article will review brain connectivity results related to the DMN in the fields of social understanding of others: emotion perception, empathy, theory...

pmc-10570809.title: Melanin: a unifying theory of disease as exemplified by Parkinson’s, Alzheimer’s, and Lewy body dementia
pmc-10570809.creator: Stacie Z. Berg, Jonathan Berg
pmc-10570809.description: Melanin, a ubiquitous dark pigment, plays important roles in the immune system, including scavenging reactive oxygen species formed in response to ultraviolet radiation absorption, absorbing metals, thermal regulation, drug uptake, innate immune system functions, redox, and energy transduction. Many tissue types, including brain, heart, arteries, ovaries, and others, contain melanin. Almost all cells contain precursors to melanin.

pmc-12699803.title: A prior knowledge-guided convolutional neural network model for predicting fetal brain age from MRI during second and third trimesters
pmc-12699803.creator: Fangmei Zhu, Shijie Huang, Xue Tang, Kai zhang, Jian Wang, Dinggang Shen, Zhongxiang Ding
pmc-12699803.description: BackgroundThis study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of a convolutional neural network (CNN) model in estimating fetal brain age from MRI scans during second and third trimesters.MethodsA total of 407 T2-weighted MRI including 2310 stacks in the axial, sagittal, and coronal planes were used. The average fetal brain age was 30.7 weeks (ranging from 22 to 39 weeks).

pmc-12983841.title: Conceptualisation and operationalisation of social support in health interventions: a scoping review
pmc-12983841.creator: Jessica Kersey, Sangjin Lee, Lisa Tabor Connor, Sarah Shyres, Elnaz Alimi, Noemi Rojas Serrano, Moon Young Kim, Phan Van Sang, Noelle Casem, Christian Le, Kim Lipsey, Elena Donoso Brown
pmc-12983841.description: ObjectivesSocial support influences health outcomes for individuals with chronic conditions, yet there is variability in how it is conceptualised and operationalised in health research. We examined how social support is conceptualised, measured and addressed through health interventions.DesignScoping review.Data sourcesPubMed/Medline, Elsevier EMBASE, NIBAHL and APA PsycInfo.

pmc-13360984.title: Gene burden meta‐analysis of 748 879 individuals identifies LGI1‐ADAM23 protein complex association with epilepsy
pmc-13360984.creator: Jessica Castrillon Lal, Costin Leu, Christian M Boßelmann, Alina Ivaniuk, Eduardo Pérez‐Palma, Dennis Lal
pmc-13360984.description: Epilepsy affects more than 50 million individuals globally and has a substantial genetic component that remains to be completely understood. Traditional studies have focused on severe, early onset cases enrolled through clinical or research settings. Recent biobank‐based approaches, leveraging large‐scale population datasets, offer opportunities to explore genetic associations in broader epilepsy phenotypes, including milder, later onset forms.

pmc-13570411.title: Association Between Maternal Syphilis Infection and Stillbirth Among Women Delivering at Jinja and Hoima Regional Referral Hospitals: An Unmatched Case–Control Study
pmc-13570411.creator: Daniel Mugabi, Theoneste Hakizimana, Musa Kasujja, John Yaweh, Sande George Bina, Adam Eibad, Geoffrey Okot, Neel Rajendra, Emmanuel Okurut, Dominic Byarugaba, Ronard Musinguzi, Karuna Sharma
pmc-13570411.description: Background and AimsMaternal syphilis infection remains a preventable contributor to stillbirth in low‐ and middle‐income countries. Evidence on its distribution among stillbirth deliveries, its independent association with fetal death, and the role of infection severity remains limited in Ugandan referral hospitals.
